title: Machine learning prioritizes candidate diabetic nephropathy diagnostic markers
summary: WGCNA and machine-learning analyses of expression datasets prioritized three candidate diabetic-nephropathy markers, with external expression data and single-nucleus data used for preliminary checks. The cohorts are small and retrospective; the authors note that more experiments are needed before clinical use.
ai_technology: WGCNA and multiple machine-learning methods prioritized candidate diagnostic markers from expression datasets.
organization: Department of Urology, Tianjin Medical University General Hospital, Tianjin, China

evidence.tested: The study reports three candidate markers and external expression/ROC assessment in a small dataset, with expression localization checked in single-nucleus data.
evidence.unknown: Small retrospective datasets do not establish diagnostic performance or clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: WGCNA and machine-learning methods prioritized candidate diagnostic markers from expression datasets.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text review as recorded in case evidence; record-level claim and attribution review.
